newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent falls in line with NYMEX profit taking.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent falls in line with NYMEX profit taking.

text.p: Brent crude futures prices in Asia were lower on Monday, down in line with the profit taking seen on NYMEX after the rally in global futures on Friday.
July Brent on SIMEX was last traded at $20.10 per barrel, down 25 cents from London, which rallied on Friday 86 cents to settle at $20.35.
June NYMEX crude, trading on the after-hours ACCESS system, was last traded at $21.77, down 35 cents from New York and at its intraday low.
July was last traded at $21.95, down 23 from New York but 10 cents above the intraday low on ACCESS.

Brokers said the rally on Friday had been overdone and tempted some profit taking Monday. Friday's Brent spike higher had taken prices to the top of the mid-February to late March trading range of $19.00 to $20.50.
However, brokers said they did not expect much downside, with initial support around $20.00 and then down to Friday's low of $19.60.
